articles.description:
Why every business must tailor its security strategy to its industry
Imagine this:
A mid-sized healthcare provider thought they had “decent” cybersecurity—basic antivirus, firewalls, and employee training. But one morning, they woke up to locked systems, stolen patient data, and a ransom note flashing on their screens. Within weeks, they lost patient trust, paid massive fines, and had their reputation dragged through the mud.
Their mistake? They treated cybersecurity as a one-size-fits-all solution instead of tailoring it to the sensitive nature of healthcare data.
This is the hidden truth: data security is not universal. A bank, a hospital, and an e-commerce store all face different threats—and need different strategies.

On a planet of electronics factories, the Little Prince once noticed something strange: the electricity in the walls (AC) moved like a wild baobab—twisting, reversing, never still. But the power in his rose’s glass dome (DC) flowed steady, like the desert wind at dawn. “Why the chaos?” he asked the fox.
The fox smiled. “AC is like the businessman’s stars—counted, not cared for. DC is like your rose—tamed, steady, yours.”
AC (Alternating Current) is electricity that reverses direction, peaking and dipping like a sine wave—50 or 60 times per second.
